It's not like she has someone providing for her.|One of [[Sila Kott]]'s brothers, to Sila Kott|<ref name="TLF">{{StoryCite|story=The Last Flight|book=From a Certain Point of View: Return of the Jedi|audiobook=1}}</ref>}}
'''Otor's Hub''' was a [[space station]]<ref name="Galaxy" /> located in a [[Otor's Hub system|star system]] in the [[Ojoster sector]] within an intersecting portion of the [[Outer Rim Territories]]<ref name="Systems" /> and the [[New Territories]].<ref name="New Territories" /> It was situated along the [[Hydian Way]] at the coordinates N-7 on the [[Standard Galactic Grid]].<ref name="Galaxy" /> It served as a gathering place for various [[merchant]]s and dealers of rare merchandise, most of whom dealt in the [[black market]] or the [[Slavery|slave]] market.<ref name="Inferno Squad">''[[Battlefront II: Inferno Squad]]''</ref> A [[standard year]] before the [[Clone Wars]], the [[Koorivar]] merchant [[Sheb Valaad]] set up a [[black market]] operation on Otor's Hub, which was foiled nearly four years later by the undercover [[Jedi Master]] [[Quinlan Vos]].<ref name="Dark Disciple">''[[Dark Disciple]]''</ref>

{{Station-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
Otor's Hub first appeared in the [[2015]] [[canon]] novel ''[[Dark Disciple]]'', written by [[Christie Golden]]. The novel was based on an eight-part story arc of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series that was never finished due to the series' cancellation. Otor's Hub originated in ''[[The Clone Wars: The Sith Hunters]]'', a [[2012]] [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (graphic novellas)|graphic novel]] that was part of the non-canon [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, which depicted Otor's Hub as a [[black market]] [[space station]]. However, in ''Dark Disciple'', the location's exact nature was not specified.
